editor_note: Habibti Nation is turning 5, with Luma, Paydar and Hiba Salameh on the bill.

listing.blurb: A club night at Colour Factory in Queen's Yard, Hackney Wick, marking five years of Habibti Nation. Time Out notes the venue puts female, non-binary and queer artists on its bills.

story.who: The event page presents Paydar, coming via Copenhagen from Iran, in her first UK show, with a SWANA-infused global club sound. Hiba Salameh, described there as Palestinian, blends Arabic traditions with futuristic electronics, and Özten brings Anatolian-rooted club rhythms.
story.then: The Yard Theatre's own website says the night grew from a monthly Balamii radio show. The Yard Theatre made Habibti Nation one of its residents for 2023/24, and Notion covered the third-birthday party there in July 2024. The event page mentions sold-out parties, festival stage takeovers, a Glastonbury slot and DJ workshops aimed at youngsters along the way.
story.now: The fifth-birthday party brings the Habibti Nation community together in Hackney Wick, according to the event page, and it includes an open decks slot for the community to start the night.
story.vibe: The event page promises SWANA sounds meeting UK and global club music, with mahraganat, dabke and raï alongside dembow, baile funk, breaks and UK funky. Notion's report on the third birthday described stalls selling clothing and a keffiyeh workshop.
worth_knowing: The Yard Theatre's own website describes the collective and party as showcasing underground electronic sounds from the SWANA region.
Habibti Nation has run DJ workshops for young people as well as parties, says the event page.
